title: Regional routing and data-locality guidelines (WIP)
summary: Working reference for implementing region-bound routing and data-locality controls in Private and Dedicated deployments. Focuses on operational requirements, ambiguous edge cases, telemetry signals, and customer communication for cross-border requests.
body:
Purpose:
- Capture pragmatic routing rules and operational guardrails that satisfy common regulator asks (EU, UK, CA, APAC) without requiring heavy-weight policy machinery for v1.
- Provide a testable checklist for deployments (VPC, on-prem bundle) and a prioritized list of edge cases that need legal/PO review.

High-level approach (opinionated):
1) Default routing by declared customer residency: requests with tenant.region metadata are bound to the customer region unless an explicit opt-in to cross-region routing exists.
2) On-host enforcement: ensure model inference path (request ingress, KV cache, model weights, and ephemeral logs) remains inside the declared region boundary for the request where possible.
3) Fallbacks: define and document safe fallback tiers (same-region replica, adjacent-region with strong encryption + audit, last-resort hosted fallback with explicit customer consent).

Operational primitives we rely on:
- Tenant metadata: tenant.region, tenant.allowed_cross_regions (list), tenant.require_in_region_processing (bool).
- Routing policy engine: small declarative ruleset executed at the dispatcher layer (pseudocode below).
- Region-qualified artifacts: model variant tags (e.g., model-v1-eu, model-v1-na), region-scoped KMS keys, storage buckets with lifecycle/replication disabled across regions.

Pseudocode (dispatcher layer):
- input: request (tenant_id, region_hint, api_key_location)
- tenant = lookupTenant(tenant_id)
- target_region = region_hint || tenant.region
- if tenant.require_in_region_processing == true and target_region != tenant.region:
    reject(403, "Region constraint: request must be processed in tenant region")
- if target_region not in tenant.allowed_cross_regions and target_region != tenant.region:
    escalate_to_compliance(ticket_context) 
- route_to = chooseBestReplica(target_region, tenant.fallback_policy)

Edge cases and recommended handling:
- IP-based vs declared residency: some customers have legal obligations tied to where data was collected (IP) vs where tenant is registered. Add an attribute collection_origin and prefer the strictest region.
- Cross-account customer workflows: if a customer has multiple tenants with different regions (e.g., acquisitions), require an explicit migration plan or per-request consent flag and record it.
- Model caching and KV cache leakage: ensure cached KV entries include region-scoped keys; eviction across regions is forbidden unless redaction is applied.
- Logs and traces: redact token-level content in traces before shipping to any central/global observability service. Keep full logs in-region for the retention window; forward aggregated metrics only.

Telemetry and SLOs to monitor (initial list):
- Percentage of requests served outside tenant.region (goal < 0.1% for strict tenants).
- Number of automatic fallbacks triggered (count and top reasons).
- Latency delta when enforcing strict in-region routing vs best-effort routing.
- KV cache hit rate per region and cross-region cache misses.
- Audit log delivery latency for region-bound events.

Customer migration & onboarding checklist (for Private / Dedicated):
- Contracting: verify residency clause and allowed backup/DR regions (legal).
- Infra prep: provision region-scoped KMS keys and storage buckets, disable cross-region replication on customer artifacts.
- Model onboarding: create region-tagged model artifacts and tests.
- E2E tests: synthetic requests from customer-controlled IPs to validate in-region path.
- Telemetry baseline: capture 7-day baseline of normal traffic distribution before enabling enforcement.
- Cutover plan: schedule migration window, communicate expected behavior and monitoring links.

Failure modes & runbook snippets:
- Scenario: Dispatcher routes to wrong region due to stale tenant metadata
  - Immediate action: disable cross-region routing via global kill-switch, open incident, roll back recent tenant metadata change, run metadata reconciliation job.
  - Post-mortem hooks: determine source of metadata drift (API, manual script, sync failure).

- Scenario: Model variant missing in target region
  - Action: fallback to region-compatible variant if allowed, otherwise enqueue a region replication job and return 503 with human-readable explanation and an estimated retry.

- Scenario: Audit logs inadvertently forwarded to global observability
  - Action: remove ingest keys immediately, revoke forwarding permissions, fetch in-region copies, notify legal and impacted customers if required.

Testing matrix (examples):
- Unit tests: rule engine for 30+ permutations of tenant flags, region hints, and fallback policies.
- Integration tests: deploy a minimal stack in two region replicas and run scripted requests asserting routing decisions and cache boundaries.
- E2E: invite a friendly customer for an on-site verification (VPN into their VPC + public endpoint simulation).

Open questions for Legal / Product:
- Do regulators in scope allow encrypted cross-border processing if customer data is always encrypted with customer-managed key (bring-your-own-kms)? (We should get a written position.)
- Acceptable audit window for replicated telemetry (aggregates ok, traces not ok?)
- Explicit consent model: is an opt-in checkbox during tenant creation sufficient for cross-region fallback?

Implementation notes for infra engineers:
- Do not rely on IP geolocation for final enforcement. Use tenant.shipping_address.region (explicit) as authority.
- Use immutable region tag baked into tenant config snapshots; changes should create a migration task, not an immediate switch.
- KMS: prefer per-region customer CMKs where supported; fallback to wrapped keys stored in-region.

Customer communication template (short):
- "Hello <customer>, we’re preparing your private deployment to respect data-locality. During the migration window (T), your requests will be routed to region R and some features (cross-region backup) will be temporarily disabled. Contact your account team if you require a different configuration"

Appendix: useful references and tickets
- Confluence: overview page (linked above)
- Jira: JIRA-ENG-4823 (region dispatcher prototype), JIRA-SEC-99 (audit forwarding review)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/712 - initial region tags implementation

Quick TODO (next 6 weeks):
- Lock down dispatcher kill-switch and add a forced in-region mode flag (owner: Liam).
- Add telemetry dashboards for "requests served outside tenant.region" (owner: Asha).
- Legal: confirm BYOK cross-border processing acceptability for EU (owner: Priya, action: schedule call w/ counsel).
- Draft customer-facing migration email and include opt-in language (owner: Diego).

Notes to self (handy reminders):
- Keep the rule engine small and auditable; avoid introducing too many exception paths.
- Document all fallbacks in the product console so customers can see route history.
- Expect 2–3 iterations after pilot customers sign off; plan for backward compatibility flags.

---
End of WIP.
